findings.location: platforms/claude-code/commands/next-loop.md (Step 6/7, unchanged by this branch) vs platforms/claude-code/agents/ralph-loop-worker.md (lines 18, 48-50, 189, 246, edited by this branch)
findings.description: The controller-worker boundary rewrite (loop-006-1) is incomplete and self-contradictory for the Claude Code adapter, which is the one adapter with an actual executable orchestration flow. ralph-loop-worker.md was edited to state that the worker does NOT write programme state (loop-complete.json, loop-ready.json, PLANNING.md, history.jsonl) and instead emits a collected-evidence document, with the controller writing programme state from that evidence. next-loop.md, the command that spawns this exact worker and consumes its output, was not touched by loop-006-1 (only loop-006-3 added an unrelated 7a block to it), and Step 6 of next-loop.md still says the worker will write .advanced-plans/state/loop-complete.json, with Step 7 doing a bare cat of that same file. No file anywhere in the repository shows code or a documented step that turns a worker collected-evidence document into loop-complete.json for this adapter. If a ralph-loop-worker session follows its own updated instructions, next-loop.md Step 7 and 7a will find no file. next-phase.md has the identical unrepaired assumption at its own Step 5. No test cross-checks consistency between the agent-definition files and the command files that actually drive them.
findings.evidence: git diff origin/main..HEAD limited to platforms/claude-code/commands/next-loop.md shows only the 7a insertion, none of Steps 6 or 7. next-loop.md still reads: The worker will write .advanced-plans/state/loop-complete.json, and then cat .advanced-plans/state/loop-complete.json. ralph-loop-worker.md line 18 reads: I do NOT write programme state (loop-complete.json, loop-ready.json, PLANNING.md, history.jsonl). The controller writes these from the collected-evidence document I emit. Searching next-loop.md for the phrase collected-evidence returns zero matches. next-phase.md has the same unrepaired Writes loop-complete.json / Read loop-complete.json pair.

findings.description: The phase-6 success criterion about a worker attempting a planning-state edit failing collection (ACC-08) has no live enforcement anywhere in the shipped system. scope_policy.py and the three-gate path in evidence_gate.py (validate_advancement and can_advance_loop, the only functions that call validate_path_scope) are fully implemented and covered by dozens of unit tests, but neither function is called from any production code path: searching the whole repository, excluding the module itself and its own tests, for validate_advancement, can_advance_loop or scope_policy finds nothing outside the module docstring example and CHANGELOG.md prose. The only wired call from a real workflow is next-loop.md Step 7a, which invokes validate_loop_complete_advancement, the two-gate path, whose own docstring states plainly that it does not check path scope because loop-complete.json carries no changed_paths field, and that there is no commit-stage path-scope enforcement today. The project own evidence file for loop-006-3 independently reaches the same conclusion, labelled finding F37, but the gap is carried rather than closed in this branch. CHANGELOG.md entry for evidence_gate.py states that collected evidence advances a loop only when schema validation and the policy gates and path scope all pass, and describes this as invoked from next-loop.md at step 7a in the same paragraph, which conflates the two gate functions and overstates what step 7a actually checks.
findings.evidence: Searching for validate_advancement or can_advance_loop across all files except evidence_gate.py and its tests returns only CHANGELOG.md. evidence_gate.py docstring for validate_loop_complete_advancement states: Path scope is NOT validated because loop-complete.json does not contain changed_paths, and there is no commit-stage path-scope enforcement today. next-loop.md calls validate_loop_complete_advancement, not validate_advancement. The evidence file at .advanced-plans/evidence/2026-09-01-loop-006-3-advancement-gate-executed.md, finding F37, corroborates the same gap from the controller own record.

findings.description: The assert-the-negative tests that loop-006-2 own checks required (assert the negative too, that programme state is unchanged after the failed collection) are vacuous. validate_path_scope(changed_paths, allowed_paths, forbidden_paths) is a pure function over lists of path strings and never opens, reads or writes any file. Each test in this class writes bytes to a tmp_path file, calls validate_path_scope with unrelated string arguments, then re-reads the same file and asserts the bytes are unchanged. That assertion is guaranteed to hold for any implementation of validate_path_scope, including one that always returns a constant, because the function is never given the file path and cannot touch it. Ran the three tests standalone and confirmed they pass in isolation. This is the exact check that cannot fail defect class the phase exists to eliminate, reproduced inside the very test suite meant to prove it was closed. It is a lower-severity finding than the two above because there is currently no real state-writing code path for it to have missed, per the first finding above, but as written it would not catch a real regression if one existed.
findings.evidence: scope_policy.py validate_path_scope signature takes only changed_paths, allowed_paths and forbidden_paths, no file path argument. Running pytest against TestNegativeAssertion_StateUnchangedOnFailure in isolation shows all 3 tests pass in 0.60 seconds.

findings.description: platforms/cursor and setup/cursor are still absent from DEFAULT_SCANNED_ROOTS after this branch, so roughly 2200 lines of newly shipped Cursor adapter code (install.sh, install.ps1, uninstall.sh, uninstall.ps1, README.md) are not examined by the path-convention or host-neutrality audit at all. This was named as a carried gap in loop-004-3 and loop-005-2 own evidence records and remains unresolved two loops later. It is honestly disclosed in CHANGELOG.md and in docs/adapting-to-new-platforms.md, so this is a transparency gap rather than a concealment. It does not break the specific phase criterion about core/, which is scanned and enforced correctly, confirmed here by running path_audit and by the existing loop-003 mutation test, but it does mean the audits coverage of the five shipped adapters is four of five.
findings.evidence: Running python -m platforms.python.path_audit from the reviewed worktree reports scanned roots that list setup/codex and setup/opencode but not setup/cursor or platforms/cursor. The CHANGELOG.md 0.20.0 entry explicitly names the gap as still open.

findings.location: platforms/claude-code/agents/ralph-orchestrator.md, description line, line 18, and Hard Contract clause (e) around line 35
findings.description: The boundary text injected into this file appears to have been pasted without adapting it to the file own role. The frontmatter description and line 18 both say that the orchestrator is the writer of programme state including loop-ready.json, while the newly added clause (e) says the controller writes loop-ready.json, loop-complete.json, PLANNING.md and history.jsonl from the worker collected-evidence, and that the orchestrator does not write these directly. loop-ready.json is prepared by the orchestrator before any worker has run, so it cannot be derived from a worker collected-evidence, which only exists after a worker finishes. The clause as written does not describe how loop-ready.json is actually produced. This looks like a mechanical batch edit (commit 071d005 is titled batch 3 of 3) that did not fully account for this file distinct role relative to the worker prompts it was copied alongside.
findings.evidence: platforms/claude-code/agents/ralph-orchestrator.md lines 2 and 18, and Hard Contract clause (e), quoted verbatim in the description above.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Every target host discovers the same named core planning skills, not host-specific copies that drift.
criteria_outcomes.evidence: loop-005-4 own fixture run found byte-identical content for the seven shared skill names across all four hosts, but found that skill resolution differs by host (opencode resolves the claude-code copy instead of its own, cursor never listed one shared skill at all), and that the checklist could not fully be honoured under a fake HOME on three of four hosts. This is carried as a set of named findings, not silently passed.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: A fixture programme can create one phase, one loop, and one external task on every target host.
criteria_outcomes.evidence: loop-004-4 exercised opencode fully, phase, loop and validated envelope, but codex only reached phase creation before stopping at a human-authorised quota decision. loop-005-3 exercised cursor through phase and loop creation but the envelope-emission step was blocked by a machine-level shell-hook incompatibility and honestly recorded as blocked rather than faked.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Only the control checkout updates programme state; a worker attempting a planning-state edit fails collection (ACC-08).
criteria_outcomes.evidence: scope_policy.py and evidence_gate.py three-gate path implement and unit-test this rule correctly in isolation, but no production code path in the repository calls validate_advancement or can_advance_loop. The one wired call, next-loop.md step 7a via validate_loop_complete_advancement, explicitly does not check path scope. See the corresponding critical finding above.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Collected evidence advances a loop only after both schema validation and gate validation pass.
criteria_outcomes.evidence: validate_loop_complete_advancement two gates, schema via state_validate and policy gates via codex_gate.aggregate_verdicts, are each proven independently in test_evidence_gate.py, and the call is pinned into next-loop.md step 7a by a test that reads the command file off disk. This mechanism is sound on its own terms; its dependency on loop-complete.json actually existing is put at risk by the first critical finding above.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: The CI path audit fails on any host-specific path in core/.
criteria_outcomes.evidence: Running python -m platforms.python.path_audit against the reviewed worktree scans core/agents and core/skills, applies the core-scoped host-neutrality rule from loop-003, and reports a pass with 7 named, reasoned exceptions in core/skills/permission-config/SKILL.md, none of which involve the edits made in this branch. No new host token was introduced under core/ by any of the 20 reviewed commits.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: No adapter duplicates a core skill content; adapters install and register, they do not fork.
criteria_outcomes.evidence: setup/cursor/install.sh sources skills from platforms/shared/agent-skills/advanced-planning and core/skills at install time with no inlined skill content, confirmed by reading the script. The adapter was derived from setup/opencode/ by measured, minimal token substitution, 62 of 774, 38 of 532, 26 of 387 and 24 of 323 changed lines, rather than rewritten from scratch.

failure_notes: Update platforms/claude-code/commands/next-loop.md and next-phase.md so the Claude Code adapter actual orchestration flow implements, or at minimum does not contradict, the worker-emits-collected-evidence and controller-writes-loop-complete.json contract that ralph-loop-worker.md and ralph-orchestrator.md now describe. Today the command files still instruct the worker to write loop-complete.json directly and read it with a bare cat.

Wire evidence_gate.validate_advancement, the three-gate path that includes scope_policy.validate_path_scope, into at least one real collection or advancement code path, so ACC-08 and ACC-13 are enforced by something an actual worker run reaches, not only by a unit test that constructs the inputs itself.

Replace or supplement TestNegativeAssertion_StateUnchangedOnFailure in test_scope_policy.py with a test that exercises real state-writing code, since validate_path_scope never touches the filesystem and the current tests cannot fail regardless of the implementation under test.
Add platforms/cursor and setup/cursor to path_audit.py DEFAULT_SCANNED_ROOTS, a gap already disclosed as carried across two prior loops.
Correct the CHANGELOG.md entry for evidence_gate.py so it does not imply that path-scope checking is part of what next-loop.md step 7a enforces.
